Rashi on Megillah 2a:10:1.english: And still it is needed - This [fact] that it used 'times' in the plural.

Rashi on Megillah 2a:10:2.hebrew: זמנו - של מוקפין לאו כזמנו של פרזים, דאי כתוב בזמן, הוה משמע זמן אחד לשניהן — אי בעו ליקרו בארביסר, ואי בעו ליקרו בחמיסר:
Rashi on Megillah 2a:10:2.english: The time of [this one] - [That] of walled [cities] is not like the time of unwalled [cities], for had it written "at the time," it would have implied one time for both of them: if they wish, let them read on the fourteenth, and if they wish, let them read on the fifteenth.

Rashi on Megillah 2a:11:1.hebrew: זמניהם דומיא דזמנם - רבויא דדרשינן לקרא לייתורא דיו"ד וה"א, דומיא דעיקר הזמן דנפקא לן מזמנם הוא דקא מרבה, דומיא דידהו:
Rashi on Megillah 2a:11:1.english: “Their times” [is] similar to “their time” - The inclusion that we expound from the verse due to the surplus of the *yod* and *heh* — it is [only an addition] similar to the primary time that is derived for us from “their time” that it includes, [namely,] similar to them [two days].

Rashi on Megillah 2a:12:1.hebrew: זמן קהלה לכל היא - הכל נקהלו להנקם מאויביהם, בין בשושן בין בשאר מקומות, כמו שכתוב בספר. הלכך, לא צריך קרא לרבויי שיהא ראוי לקרייה, דעיקר הנס בו היה:
Rashi on Megillah 2a:12:1.english: It is a time of assembly for all - Everyone assembled to avenge themselves on their enemies, both in Shushan and in other places, as it is written in the Book [of Esther]. Therefore, a verse is not needed to include [it to establish] that it is fit for reading [the Megillah], since the main miracle occurred on it.

Rashi on Megillah 2a:14:1.hebrew: ימים כימים - לעיל מיניה כתיב י"ד וט"ו ישמחו, וכתיב כימים אשר נחו בהם היהודים וגו'. והוה ליה למיכתב ימים אשר נחו, דמשמע: הם הם ימים אשר נחו. מאי כימים? לרבות שנים אחרות כדוגמתן:
Rashi on Megillah 2a:14:1.english: Days, as the days - Earlier in the passage, it is written that [on the] fourteenth and fifteenth they shall rejoice, and it is written: “As the days on which the Jews rested [from their enemies]...” And it should have written: “the days on which they rested,” which would imply the very days on which they rested. What [then is the meaning of] “as the days”? To include other years like them.

Rashi on Megillah 2a:17:1.hebrew: לדורות הוא דכתיב - להכי שייך לישנא דקרא כימים, כלומר: יעשו לדורות י"ד וט"ו כאשר היה בימי הנס — ימים אשר נחו בהם. הלכך, לא איכא לרבויי מהכא שנים אחרים:
Rashi on Megillah 2a:17:1.english: It is written for [future] generations - It is for this [reason] that the wording of the verse "as the days" is appropriate, that is to say: they shall observe for [future] generations the fourteenth and fifteenth [of Adar], just as it was in the days of the miracle — [the] days on which they rested. Therefore, there is no [basis] to include two other [days] from here.

Rashi on Megillah 2a:18:1.english: This is the statement of Rabbi Akiva - This is what Rabbi Yochanan learned from his teacher: that Rabbi Akiva stated our Mishnah.

Rashi on Megillah 2a:18:2.hebrew: סתימתאה - הרבה סתם משנה סתם ר', שהן דברי ר' עקיבא. וי"מ סתימתאה: כל הסתומין תלמידיו היו, כדאמר בסנהדרין (דף פו.): סתם משנה — ר"מ, סתם תוספתא — ר' נחמיה, סתם ספרא — רבי יהודה, וכולהו סתימתאי — אליבא דר' עקיבא. אך קשה בעיני לפרש כן, שמצינו בכמה מקומות בשם ר"א בר' יוסי סתימתאי, רבי מנחם בר רבי יוסי סתימתאי לקמן בפרק בני העיר (מגילה דף כו.):
Rashi on Megillah 2a:18:2.english: The unattributed one - Rebbi taught many unattributed Mishnayot that are the words of Rabbi Akiva. And some explain [the epithet] "the unattributed one": All the authors of unattributed [compilations] were his disciples, as [the Gemara] says in Sanhedrin (86a): An unattributed Mishnah is Rabbi Meir; an unattributed Tosefta is Rabbi Nechemiah; an unattributed Sifra is Rabbi Yehudah; and all these unattributed [compilations] follow Rabbi Akiva. However, it is difficult in my view to explain this way, for we find in several places: [cited] in the name of Rabbi Elazar bar Rabbi Yose, "the unattributed one", and "Rabbi Menachem bar Rabbi Yose, the unattributed one" below in the chapter "Benei Ha'Ir" (Megillah 26a).

Rashi on Megillah 2a:19:1.english: When - [did] the Sages show leniency to the villages?

Rashi on Megillah 2a:19:2.hebrew: בזמן שהשנים כתיקנן - שהשנים מתעברות על פי בית דין, והחדשים המקדשין בבית דין שולחין שלוחיהן להודיע אימתי הוקדש ניסן, ועושין מועדים ע"פ שלוחין:
Rashi on Megillah 2a:19:2.english: At a time when the years are established properly - That the years are intercalated by the court, and [for] the months that are sanctified in court, they send their messengers to make known when Nisan was sanctified, and they observe the festivals according to the messengers.

Rashi on Megillah 2a:19:3.english: When they dwell upon their land - And the messengers reach the edge of the Land of Israel by Passover.

Rashi on Megillah 2a:19:4.hebrew: אבל בזמן הזה - שפסקו כל אלה, וישראל נפרדו, ולא יגיעו שלוחי ב"ד אצלם — הכל צופין למקרא מגילה, ואומרים: יום י"ד באדר קרינן המגילה, נשארו לאדר ט"ו יום, וט"ו של ניסן עושין פסח. ואם תקדים קריאתה, יעשו פסח לסוף שלשים יום של קריאה, ונמצאו אוכלין חמץ בימים אחרונים (ביום) של פסח:
Rashi on Megillah 2a:19:4.english: However, nowadays - Since all these [conditions] have ceased, and the Jewish people are dispersed, and the emissaries of the court do not reach them — everyone looks to the reading of the Megillah, and they say: "On the fourteenth day of Adar we read the Megillah; fifteen days remain in Adar, and on the fifteenth of Nisan we celebrate Passover." And if you advance its reading, they will celebrate Passover at the end of thirty days from the reading, and they will end up eating chametz on the final days (on the day) of Passover.

Rashi on Megillah 2a:1:1.hebrew: מגילה נקראת בי"א וכו' - פעמים בזה ופעמים בזה, ולקמן מפרש ואזיל:
Rashi on Megillah 2a:1:1.english: The Megillah is read on the eleventh, etc. - Sometimes on this [day] and sometimes on that [day], and further on [the mishna] proceeds to explain.

Rashi on Megillah 2a:1:2.english: Not earlier and not later - Not earlier than the eleventh, and not later than the fifteenth.

Rashi on Megillah 2a:1:3.english: From the days of Joshua - In the Gemara it explains this.

Rashi on Megillah 2a:1:4.hebrew: אלא שהכפרים מקדימין ליום הכניסה - כלומר, מאחר שהמוקפין קורין בט"ו ושאין מוקפין קורין בי"ד — הרי הכל בכלל. תו, היכי משכחת י"א, י"ב, י"ג? אלא שהכפרים — נתנו להן חכמים רשות להקדים קריאתה ליום הכניסה: יום שני בשבת שלפני י"ד או חמישי בשבת, שהוא יום כניסה, שהכפרים מתכנסין לעיירות למשפט, לפי שבתי דינין יושבין בעיירות בשני ובחמישי כתקנת עזרא (ב"ק דף פב.). והכפרים אינן בקיאין לקרות, וצריכין שיקראנה להם אחד מבני העיר, ולא הטריחום חכמים להתאחר ולבא ביום י"ד. ופעמים שיום הכניסה בי"ג, ופעמים שהוא בי"א:
Rashi on Megillah 2a:1:4.english: However, the villages advance [their reading] to the day of assembly - That is to say, since walled [cities] read on the fifteenth and those that are not walled read on the fourteenth, behold, everyone is included. Furthermore, how do you find [the reading occurring on] the eleventh, the twelfth, [or] the thirteenth? Rather, [as for] the villages, the Sages gave them permission to advance its reading to the day of assembly: the Monday before the fourteenth, or the Thursday [before it], which is a day of assembly when the villagers gather to the towns for judgment, because the courts sit in the towns on Mondays and Thursdays according to the enactment of Ezra (Bava Kamma 82a). And the villagers are not proficient in reading [the Megillah], and need one of the townspeople to read it to them, and the Sages did not trouble them to delay and come on the fourteenth. And sometimes the day of assembly is on the thirteenth, and sometimes it is on the eleventh.

Rashi on Megillah 2a:20:1.english: Nowadays, too, this ordinance applies - For behold, Rabbi Akiva [lived] nowadays, and he said in the Mishnah that they advance [the reading].

Rashi on Megillah 2a:21:1.english: Rather, is it not in accordance with the Rabbis - He stated it [in accordance with the Rabbis] who were before Rabbi Akiva.

Rashi on Megillah 2a:21:2.english: At least we read - Evidently, the Rabbis also expound “time,” “their time,” [and] “their times”.

Rashi on Megillah 2a:22:1.hebrew: איכא דאמרי אמר רבה זו דברי ר' עקיבא סתימתאה - ולא גרסינן להאי לישנא דדריש זמן זמנם זמניהם, דהא רבנן דפליגי עליה נמי דרשי ליה, אלא שהחמירו לאחר חורבן משום דמסתכלין בה:
Rashi on Megillah 2a:22:1.english: There are those who say: Rabba said: This is the statement of Rabbi Akiva, the unattributed - And we do not read in this version, "for he expounds *zeman*, *zemanam*, *zemanehem* [time, their time, and their times]," for the Rabbis who disagree with him also expound it; rather, they were stringent after the Destruction [of the Temple] because [people] look to it.

Rashi on Megillah 2a:24:1.hebrew: קשיא דר"י - דהא ברייתא דלעיל אדר' יהודה דמתני', כדמפרש ואזיל:
Rashi on Megillah 2a:24:1.english: [The statement of] Rabbi Yehuda was difficult - For this baraita above [contradicts that of] Rabbi Yehuda of the Mishnah, as [the Gemara] proceeds to explain.

Rashi on Megillah 2a:3:1.hebrew: חל ארבעה עשר להיות בערב שבת עיירות ומוקפין חומה קורין בו ביום - שאין קריאת המגילה בשבת, גזירה שמא יטלנה בידו. וא"ת: יאחרו המוקפין עד אחר שבת? הוה ליה ט"ז, ואמר קרא: ולא יעבור:
Rashi on Megillah 2a:3:1.english: [If] the fourteenth occurs on Shabbat eve, towns and walled [cities] read on that day - For the reading of the Megillah does not [take place] on Shabbat, [as a Rabbinic] decree lest one take it in his hand [and carry it in the public domain]. And if you should say: Let the walled [cities] delay [their reading] until after Shabbat? That would be the sixteenth [of Adar], and Scripture states: "And it shall not pass."

Rashi on Megillah 2a:4:1.hebrew: חל להיות אחר שבת כפרים מקדימין ליום הכניסה - דהוה ליה י"א, וטפי לא משכחת לה יום הכניסה שלפני פורים מוקדם לו, דמיום הכניסה ליום הכניסה לא מקדמינן:
Rashi on Megillah 2a:4:1.english: [If the fourteenth] occurs after Shabbat, villages advance to the day of assembly - As this is the eleventh [of Adar], and you do not find the day of assembly preceding Purim [any] more advanced for it [than this], for from [one] day of assembly to [another] day of assembly we do not advance [the reading].

Rashi on Megillah 2a:5:2.english: So that they may supply - That they should be free on the day of Purim to supply the needs of the Purim feast for the residents of the towns.

Rashi on Megillah 2a:6:1.hebrew: אנן הכי קאמרינן - אנן, דמיבעיא לן ״מנלן״, הכי קאמרינן:
Rashi on Megillah 2a:6:1.english: This is what we are saying - We, who asked "From where do we [derive this]?", this is what we are saying:

Rashi on Megillah 2a:6:2.hebrew: מכדי - מדהקילו חכמים על הכפרים להקדים, על כרחך אנשי כנסת הגדולה — שתיקנו בימי מרדכי ואסתר את שמחת הפורים וקריאת המגילה — כולהו הני זימני תיקון, ונתנו רשות לקרות:
Rashi on Megillah 2a:6:2.english: Now - Since the Sages were lenient with the villages to advance [the reading], perforce the Men of the Great Assembly — who instituted the celebration of Purim and the reading of the Megillah in the days of Mordechai and Esther — instituted all of these times and gave permission to read [on them].

Rashi on Megillah 2a:6:3.hebrew: דאי סלקא דעתך - י"ד וט"ו תקון, הכתובין במגילה, ותו לא:
Rashi on Megillah 2a:6:3.english: For if it enters your mind - [That] they enacted the fourteenth and fifteenth, which are written in the Megillah, and nothing more.

Rashi on Megillah 2a:6:4.hebrew: היכי אתו רבנן - דבתרייהו, ועקרו תקנתא והתירו להקדים — בתמיה:
Rashi on Megillah 2a:6:4.english: How could the Sages come - [Those] who came after them, and uproot the ordinance and permit advancing [the reading]? [This is stated] in astonishment.

Rashi on Megillah 2a:7:1.hebrew: אלא פשיטא אינהו תקון - וכיון דאינהו תקון, ודאי רמזינהו במגילת אסתר. היינו דמיבעיא לן: היכא רמיזא, ומנלן:
Rashi on Megillah 2a:7:1.english: Rather, it is obvious that they enacted [them] - And since they [the Men of the Great Assembly] enacted them, they certainly alluded to them in the Scroll of Esther. That is what we were asking: "Where is it alluded to, and from where do we [derive it]?"

Rashi on Megillah 2a:9:1.english: For itself - For the fourteenth and the fifteenth, which are specified in the Book [of Esther].

Rashi on Megillah 2a:9:2.hebrew: לימא קרא - ״את ימי הפורים האלה בזמן״, דמשמע: בזמן המפורש להם:
Rashi on Megillah 2a:9:2.english: Let the verse say - "These days of Purim in [its] time," which would imply: at the time specified for them.
